meaning: to succeed in an exam or test very well
literal_translation: passar com louvor; ter um excelente desempenho em uma prova
example: She studied hard all year and passed her final exam with flying colours.
origin: Probably linked to ships or armies flying bright flags when they returned victorious; the exact origin is uncertain.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to fly a kite in the playground
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal, playful image and has nothing to do with exam results

wrong_meanings.meaning: to fail a test very badly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom means the opposite: a very good result, not a failure

wrong_meanings.meaning: to paint the classroom walls in bright colours
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The word 'colours' is used in a figurative sense here, not as a literal description of painting

explanation: 'Pass with flying colours' means to succeed very clearly and easily, usually in an exam or test. It is a positive idiom used to praise a strong result.
